overall.summary: Every number reproduces, and so do the closed forms, coverage and function preservation. Three statements are refuted: the record says normal sodium leaves all three hinges off, but the model's floor is only 135-137 mmol/L and risk climbs through upper-normal sodium; the clinical summary says a higher BMI raises the risk steadily, but for low-sodium patients the model's risk falls as BMI rises (163 training rows); and one ablation sentence reverses the direction of a small effect. Several clinical labels for thresholds ('upper end', 'middle' of the normal range) do not fit the switch-on points the record itself reports.

findings.statement: normal sodium leaves all three [hinges] off; ... a gentle one from the middle of the normal range ... a steep one from the top of the normal range
findings.check: probe sodium sweep (typical, men and women); subgroup counts on node values
findings.evidence: Over the normal range 135-145 mmol/L only 135-137 leaves all three off. The gentle hinge (219) is on from 138 (men 0.14, women 0.017) and is positive on 812 of the 812 training rows with sodium >= 139; the steep hinge is on from 142 (0.027) and at 144 is 0.47. Typical risk is 10.4% at 137 but 20.9% at 140 (mid-normal) and 79.9% at 144 (still normal). The gentle hinge starts below the middle of the range (137-138, middle 140) and the steep one 3-4 mmol/L below its top (145).

low_sodium_hinge.why: The exit tracks how far sodium falls below about 137 mmol/L, moved about 0.2 mmol/L lower per BMI unit (concept score 1.00, BMI sweeps confirm), and it reaches the prediction only below about 134.5 through the arm.

high_sodium_steep_hinge.why: The exit is the excess of sodium above about 142 mmol/L (score 0.99), slightly shifted by noise; the reading holds, only its label as 'above the normal range' is wrong.

nondiabetic_noise_chain.why: Driven by the random noise column, gated off by diabetes, with no effect on AUC; the only description is its own formula.

low_creatinine_noise_chain.why: Only the creatinine gate has a reading (on when creatinine is low, 27 of 427 rows above 100 umol/L); what passes the gate is mainly noise.

flags.note: Domain (model, not explanation): the model's lowest risk sits at 135-137 mmol/L and risk is already doubled at 140 and about 80% at 144, inside the usual 135-145 normal range; and for low-sodium patients a higher BMI lowers the predicted risk. A domain reviewer should look at both.

notes: Evidence is all on the training split (n = 1500); no test-split numbers are used as evidence. No plain-language drafts or claims exist for this genome, so sections on drafts and claims were skipped. Nothing was written to the database or the target.
